reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 states that for low-temperature syntheses 'the factors determining phase formation... are so far unclear,' directly contradicting the claimed mechanism. E2 notes that differences in reduction potentials cause phase separation but does not show that low-temperature methods overcome this; it only mentions that solvothermal methods can produce uniform bimetallic/timetallic particles, not HEA nanoparticles.
premises: Low-temperature solution reduction synchronizes reduction kinetics of noble metal precursors
Synchronized kinetics prevent premature reduction of individual metals and phase separation
High-temperature processes cause asynchronous reduction, leading to elemental segregation
